Steady clocks (std::chrono::steady_clock) are monotonic: they never jump backward or forward, unlike the system (wall) clock, which NTP adjustments, manual changes, or leap seconds can alter. Steady time measures elapsed time from an arbitrary fixed point, making it suitable for timeouts and intervals. System time reflects calendar time since the Unix epoch and can be adjusted.

Timers rely on steady time because it is monotonic: it never jumps backward or forward when the system clock is adjusted by NTP, manual changes, or daylight saving. Timer periods therefore fire reliably.
